case_name: Krishna Obroi vs Vijay Kumar Obroi
facts_of_case: Obroi knew Miss Godwani, a working girl. They underwent an alleged marriage in Arya Samaj temple on March 17, 1965. Obroi filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights against Miss Godwani alleging that the marriage was solemnized and witnessed by the Priest and other office-bearers of the Samaj.

legal_principles.principle: In the absence of a custom to the contrary, the rites essential for a Hindu marriage are two: (a) the invocation before the sacred fire, i.e., Homam; and (b) taking of seven steps round the fire by the bride and bridegroom, Saptapadi.
legal_principles.held: It is well-established that in the absence of a custom to the contrary, the rites essential for a Hindu marriage are two: namely, the invocation before the sacred lire, i.e., Homam; and (b) taking of seven steps round the fire by the bride and bridegroom, Saptapadi.
cited_cases: Bhaurao Shankar Lokhande v. The State of Maharashtra
Kanwal Ram v. The Himachal Pradesh Administration

legal_principles.principle: When a party has denied the factum of the marriage, the burden lies on the other party to prove the same.
legal_principles.held: Obroi was bound to prove the same. Against the general evidence adduced for Obroi, the specific evidence of Miss Godwani and RW. 1 Nathu Ram is that Saptapadi was not performed at all.
